rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin; a box is the screen bounding box of its 8 projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]
rules.floor: the room is built round the old picture: a place on its floor keeps its screen place. A frog place q: the floor point under (q.x + 16, q.y + 25), new q = old q. A person's place (x, y): the floor point under (x, y - 1), new (x, y) = old. So every floor position of sala.js, its stories and its pairs keeps its numbers, but for the few in moves (where the old picture put someone under the answer cards or a bubble on a face); the sheet names each one (spots, remap, code, moves) with its world point
rules.relative: what the old code draws or moves relative to a person, the frog or a point (p.x + 22, q.x + 16, h[0] - 2, the bubbles, the trays, the cups, the Z of sleep) keeps its offsets
rules.sky: screen-space effects keep their old numbers: the flash (W.flash), the blur (W.borroso), the stars of final6 and final8, the heart (heartAt)
rules.view: both views are zoom 1: the 196 x 216 window from x0 22, the old wide one. A change of view moves nothing
rules.pair: a review or level picture is pictures[word.side] (level: level[...].picture): zoom 1 = the 196 x 104 window crop; zoom 2 = the 98 x 52 crop shown nearest-neighbour at 2 x 2. The old rectangles (remap cam and crop) say which pictures they were

room.what: a doll's house cut: of the room's four walls only the two far ones stand, the left one (facing +x, in shade: the door to the porch and the three frames) and the back one (facing +y, lit: the window). The two near walls are not built. The floor runs past the picture's bottom and sides, so no cut edge of it shows; the standing walls are cut at 3.2 (a strip of wall over the door and the window), their cut tops a white edge. Furniture is turned to face the camera (as El balcón's chairs): the sofa stands across the corner, so the family sits in a row as in the old picture
room.why: the old picture is a wall and a floor that fill the frame, every place in it on that floor; a near wall, even cut low, would stand across the frog's floor and over feet, and a cut edge of the floor would be a line across the room. The two far walls are where the old door (left) and window (right) were; the corner between them is behind the sofa, as the old wall was

front.how: sala.js:114 drew the low table in the list sorted by y (its y 165): everyone whose y is less is drawn before it and covered by it. The table is in the set now; at its place in the list, for each person (and the frog) drawn before it, the set's own pixels of the table (sala-set.html part "mesita", PART_TAGS) are drawn again inside that character's box, only where that pixel is nearer to the camera than the character: bakedZ[i] > v / COS - (row + .5 - OY) * tan(30 deg) / S, v = (x + y) / R2 of the floor point under the character's feet (people: unproject(x, y - 1); the frog: unproject(q.x + 16, q.y + 25)). The cake and the camera are drawn after it, as before. "Behind the table" is that depth test, not the row
